metaDescription: Rankin, the Upton County seat, sits on the edge of the Spraberry Trend. Get a plain-spoken valuation on your mineral or royalty interest here.
heroLead: Rankin is small enough that most everyone knows most everyone, and the mineral ownership around town reflects that — a handful of ranching families whose land has stayed in the family for generations.
intro: As the Upton County seat, Rankin is where the courthouse records for the surrounding ranchland live, and a lot of that ranchland has minerals underneath it that trace back to the same original allotments settled decades ago. The Spraberry Trend runs through this part of the county, though it's less densely drilled here than it is farther north around Midland.

sections.heading: Small town, scattered small interests
paragraphs: Because Rankin's population has stayed small, mineral ownership here tends to be concentrated among a limited number of family names, but split into small fractional shares across many heirs. If you've got a piece of a Rankin-area interest that seems too small to bother with, it's still worth a quick check on current value.

sections.heading: Edge-of-core acreage means checking, not assuming
paragraphs: Rankin sits along the southern edge of the dense Spraberry development concentrated farther north, which means activity here is more selective. Some sections nearby see active horizontal drilling; others haven't been touched in years. We check current permits on your specific tract rather than pricing off the county's general reputation.

sections.heading: What ranching-family title looks like around Rankin
paragraphs: Because so much of Upton County's land has stayed with the original settling families, title around Rankin often runs through wills and informal family agreements rather than clean recorded deeds. Heirship affidavits and probate filings at the county clerk's office are common tools for tracing ownership when a family never formally divided an inherited mineral interest.

None of that should stop you from finding out what your share is worth. We regularly work through exactly this kind of title picture and can usually purchase your undivided interest without needing every relative to sign off first.

faqs.question: Is my small Rankin-area interest even worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Small fractional interests are common around Rankin given the concentrated family ownership here, and buyers regularly purchase interests of any size.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Rankin right now?
faqs.answer: It varies by section since Rankin sits on the edge of the denser Spraberry core to the north. We check current permitting near your specific tract before quoting anything.

faqs.question: How do I get started if my paperwork on this interest is limited?
faqs.answer: Send whatever you have and we'll confirm the rest through Upton County clerk records in Rankin.

faqs.question: My family's mineral interest near Rankin was never formally divided among the heirs. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It's common and workable. We use heirship affidavits and probate records to confirm your specific share, and we can typically purchase it without requiring the rest of the family to act at the same time.
